run.question: I have a slow query on the 'app-191-profile' index. Use the profile option to analyze this query and tell me the query type used: {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}}

report.summary: The index app-191-profile exists (green/open, 6 documents, 7.1kb) and maps message as text, status as keyword and timestamp as date. I ran the supplied wildcard query with profile:true (size 1, source filtered to message, time_field timestamp because the index has no @timestamp). In the returned profile the DSL query type is wildcard ({"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}}), and Lucene rewrote that clause into a MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper (description "message:*timeout*") nested inside a BooleanQuery inside a ConstantScoreQuery that also carries the tool's own timestamp range clause (IndexOrDocValuesQuery). A separate TermQuery "message:timeout" also appears in the profile's query list. So the answer to the question is: the query type used is wildcard, executed as a constant-score multi-term (wildcard) query over the analyzed text field message. Regarding the 'slow query' premise: this run was not slow — took 18 ms, query phase 0.47 ms, timed_out false, 3 documents matched and 1 shown. The profile records build_scorer 422,034 ns under the ConstantScoreQuery as its largest single component, consistent with the leading-wildcard term expansion, but no baseline or large-data measurement in this Run shows that this pattern causes the slowness the user reports.

claims.text: Index app-191-profile exists and is open with health green, 6 documents and 7.1kb store size.

The app-191-profile mapping has message: text, status: keyword, timestamp: date; because there is no @timestamp, the search required time_field=timestamp and the tool applied an unavoidable timestamp range filter ending 2026-11-21T05:18:50+00:00 and starting 2026-11-21T04:18:50+00:00.

With profile:true the search succeeded: shards 1 successful / 0 failed, took 18 ms, timed_out false, total 3 documents matched (relation eq) and 1 shown; the shown document (_id k_iK_KEBFz7Q4KB33ku-) has message "Socket timeout during file upload" and sort/timestamp 1795238220000.

The profile's main query is type ConstantScoreQuery wrapping type BooleanQuery whose description is "#message:*timeout* #IndexOrDocValuesQuery(indexQuery=timestamp:[1795234730000 TO 1795238330999], dvQuery=timestamp:[1795234730000 TO 1795238330999])", taking 471,938 ns in total.

The wildcard clause appears in the profile as Lucene type MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper with description "message:*timeout*" and time_in_nanos 217,549 (build_scorer 207,851 ns, create_weight 4,458 ns, build_scorer_count 3, match_count 0, next_doc_count 4) — i.e. the wildcard DSL query is executed as a constant-score multi-term query, not as a term or match query.

The profile's searches[0].query array also contains a second, separate query entry of type TermQuery with description "message:timeout" (time_in_nanos 50,414); its origin is not identified in the returned evidence.

Collector-side timings in the same profile: QueryPhaseCollector 159,261 ns (SimpleFieldCollector search_top_hits 86,304 ns, AggregatorCollector for opspilot_source_time_min/opspilot_source_time_max 59,964 ns); rewrite_time 93,946 ns on the shard.
The premise that this execution is slow is not supported by this Run's profile: the whole search took 18 ms with no timeout, on a single shard of an index containing only 6 documents.

The pattern "*timeout*" has a leading wildcard and runs against an analyzed text field, so the wildcard must expand across terms and cannot use an indexed prefix; the profile's build_scorer time under the MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper is where that cost appears. This is a plausible explanation for slowness on a larger index, but this Run has no larger-data or baseline measurement to confirm it as the cause of the reported slowness.

The extra TermQuery "message:timeout" visible in the profiled query list may come from a component added by the query path outside the user-supplied DSL (for example a source/highlight/rescore layer); the returned evidence does not show what generated it.

If the goal is to make this pattern fast at scale, consider indexing the relevant field as keyword (or a keyword sub-field) and using a normalized term/phrase match instead of a leading-wildcard expression such as "*timeout*"; verify with a profile on representative data volume before changing anything.

next_steps: Re-run the same profiled query against a representative (production-sized) index or time range and compare per-clause build_scorer/next_doc timings to establish whether the leading-wildcard expansion is the dominant cost.
Confirm which client or template emits the extra "message:timeout" term clause seen in the profile.
If slowness is confirmed at scale, evaluate converting message to a keyword sub-field with a normalized term query, and validate with a new profile before rollout.
